meta.title: Evolution of NLP — 1950 to 2030
meta.subtitle: From Shannon's information theory to agentic AI — the eight-decade journey of natural language processing

eras.label: Foundations Era
eras.summary: The pre-statistical decades. Hand-crafted linguistic rules, pattern matching, the first chatbots, and the founding debates of AI. The field's appetite for symbolic representations and finite automata set the stage for everything that came later.

milestones.title: Shannon's Information Theory Applied to Language
milestones.author: Claude Shannon, Bell Labs
milestones.summary: Claude Shannon published 'Prediction and Entropy of Printed English' in the Bell System Technical Journal, applying his recently-developed information theory to natural language. He modeled English as a stochastic process and demonstrated that languages have ~50% redundancy — the next letter can be predicted with ~50% accuracy from context. He also computed entropy rates of English at ~1.5 bits per character.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Founded the entire field of statistical language modeling. The n-gram, the perplexity metric, and information-theoretic complexity measures all descend directly from this work. Every modern LM (BERT, GPT, the phone's autocomplete) is a direct descendant of Shannon's 1950 insight.

milestones.title: Georgetown-IBM Experiment — First Public MT Demo
milestones.author: Leon Dostert (Georgetown), Cuthbert Hurd (IBM)
milestones.summary: On January 7, 1954, IBM's 701 mainframe translated 49 hand-selected Russian sentences into English at a press conference in New York. The system used 6 grammar rules and 250 lexical items, with vocabulary limited to organic chemistry. Despite the brittleness, the demonstration launched the field of machine translation.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Sparked the American and Soviet enthusiasm for machine translation that funded DARPA, NSF, and ARPA research for the next decade. The system was primitive but the public demonstration set expectations for what 'thinking machines' could do. The 1966 ALPAC report that defunded MT traced directly back to this over-promise.

milestones.title: Dartmouth Workshop — Founding of AI
milestones.author: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon, Nathaniel Rochester
milestones.summary: The 1956 Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence ran for ~2 months at Dartmouth College with 10 attendees. The proposal, written by McCarthy, coined the term 'artificial intelligence' itself. The workshop featured Allen Newell and Herbert Simon presenting the Logic Theorist — the first symbolic AI program that proved 38 of the first 52 theorems in Principia Mathematica.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Founding ceremony of AI as an academic field. NLP research for the next 65 years can be traced back to positions taken at Dartmouth: the symbolic vs. connectionist debate, the question of whether machine learning is possible, the role of formal logic in language understanding, and the role of statistical methods.

milestones.title: Syntactic Structures (Chomsky)
milestones.author: Noam Chomsky, MIT
milestones.summary: Chomsky's Syntactic Structures introduced generative grammar, the distinction between competence and performance, and finite-state vs. context-free grammars as the formal basis for syntax. The book rejected the behaviorist tradition dominant in linguistics and established formal language theory as the foundation of syntactic research.
milestones.why_it_mattered: The Chomsky hierarchy (regular, context-free, context-sensitive, recursively enumerable) became the standard classification for natural language grammars. CFGs underpin the ATN parsers of the 1970s, the Penn Treebank (1989-1993), and statistical parsers of the 1990s. Even modern dependency parsers trace their lineage to Chomsky's formal language theory.

milestones.title: ALPAC Report — The MT Winter Begins
milestones.author: Automatic Language Processing Advisory Committee (ALPAC), National Academy of Sciences
milestones.summary: The 1966 ALPAC report, 'Languages and Machines: Computers in Translation and Linguistics', was a National Academy of Sciences evaluation of machine translation. It concluded that MT was slower, less accurate, and more expensive than human translation, and that 'there is no immediate or predictable prospect of useful machine translation.' The report's recommendation cut US government MT funding dramatically.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Created the 'AI winter' for MT research that lasted until the 1980s. Indirectly, it forced the field to focus on deeper computational linguistics — ATN parsing, semantic representations, conceptual dependency — instead of superficial rule-based MT. The pendulum-back in 1990s (statistical MT) and again in 2010s (neural MT) eventually vindicated the researchers ALPAC had defunded.

milestones.title: ELIZA — The First Chatbot
milestones.author: Joseph Weizenbaum, MIT
milestones.summary: ELIZA, written by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT, was the first program to attempt human-like conversation. Using simple pattern matching and substitution rules with the DOCTOR script, ELIZA simulated a Rogerian psychotherapist. It famously fooled users into believing it understood them — now known as the 'ELIZA effect'.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Founded the field of human-computer conversation. Modern chatbots, virtual assistants, and customer service bots all trace their lineage to ELIZA. Weizenbaum's distress at users' emotional attachment to his program also planted the earliest seeds of AI ethics.

milestones.title: SHRDLU — Grounded Language Understanding
milestones.author: Terry Winograd, MIT
milestones.summary: SHRDLU was an early natural-language understanding program. The user conversed with the computer about a 'blocks world' — moving cubes, naming collections, asking about state. Combined syntax, semantics, and a simulated robot that could actually act. SHRDLU was a masterwork of integrated AI — and a casualty of the AI winter.
milestones.why_it_mattered: First system to tightly integrate parsing, semantics, and action in one coherent demo. Showed that grounded language understanding was possible in restricted domains. Inspired a generation of robotics + NLP research, including modern instruction-following agents and embodied AI.

milestones.title: Conceptual Dependency Theory
milestones.author: Roger Schank, Stanford/Yale
milestones.summary: Conceptual Dependency (CD) theory was a model of language understanding where the meaning of any sentence is reduced to a small set of primitive 'conceptual acts' (PTRANS, ATRANS, MTRANS, etc.). Two sentences with the same meaning get the same representation, regardless of surface wording. Two sentences that mean different things get different representations.
milestones.why_it_mattered: First serious attempt to capture meaning independent of the words used. Inspired a generation of story-understanding systems (MARGIE, SAM, PAM, TaleSpin). CD formalization paved the way for the structured representations used in modern knowledge graphs and semantic role labeling.

milestones.title: Augmented Transition Networks (ATNs)
milestones.author: William A. Woods, BBN
milestones.summary: Woods proposed ATNs as an extension of finite-state transition networks with arbitrary recursive structure and conditions on transitions. ATNs became the dominant parsing formalism for NLP through the 1970s and 1980s. They allowed hierarchical structures to be parsed with deterministic or non-deterministic finite-state machines.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made it tractable to write grammars for real natural-language input. ATNs were used in LUNAR (a natural-language interface to a database about moon rocks) and SHRDLU's successor systems. The algorithmic insight — recursive conditions on transitions — anticipated by 30 years the architecture of transition-based neural parsers of the 2010s.

milestones.title: MARGIE → SAM → PAM → TaleSpin
milestones.author: Schank's group at Yale (Lehnert, Wilensky, Meehan, Cullingford)
milestones.summary: A family of conceptual-dependency-based programs that could infer, paraphrase, summarize, plan, and even tell stories. MARGIE inferred implications; SAM (Script Applier Mechanism) accessed stereotyped event sequences; PAM (Plan Applier Mechanism) understood stories by recognizing the plan being executed; TaleSpin generated short folk tales about bears and bees.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Demonstrated that deep semantic representations could support reasoning and generation — not just parsing. The Yale school defined NLP research for the late 1970s and inspired the frame-based and script-based approaches that later became FrameNet and modern knowledge graphs.

milestones.title: Penn Treebank — Annotated Corpus Era Begins
milestones.author: Mitchell Marcus, Beatrice Santorini, Mary Ann Marcinkiewicz — University of Pennsylvania
milestones.summary: The Penn Treebank project published 4.5 million words of American English annotated with phrase-structure parse trees, part-of-speech tags, and other linguistic annotations. The Treebank had a transformative effect on NLP — for the first time, researchers could train statistical models on large, consistent corpora.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Created the modern paradigm of corpus-based NLP. Every statistical parsing model from 1990 onward (including the modern neural parsers) was trained on the Penn Treebank or its descendants. The Treebank also popularized the principle that scientific NLP requires shared, annotated datasets as benchmarks.

eras.label: Statistical Era
eras.summary: Hand-written rules couldn't scale. Researchers turned to probability theory, large corpora, and statistical learning. N-gram language models, HMMs for POS tagging and speech, and the first web-scale MT systems.

milestones.title: Elman Networks — Early RNN for NLP
milestones.author: Jeffrey Elman, UCSD
milestones.summary: A simple recurrent neural network that learned to predict the next word in a sequence. Each word in the training corpus was encoded as a learned vector — an early form of word embedding. The network had 20-100 hidden units and was trained on ~100 sentences.
milestones.why_it_mattered: First demonstration that neural networks could learn distributed word representations and temporal patterns from raw text. The seed of all later neural NLP work.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: LSTM — Long Short-Term Memory
milestones.author: Sepp Hochreiter & Jürgen Schmidhuber
milestones.summary: A recurrent unit with a cell state and three gates (input, output, forget) that mitigates the vanishing-gradient problem and lets RNNs learn dependencies thousands of steps long.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made RNNs actually trainable on long sequences. Dominant sequence model for speech, MT, and text generation from 2010 through 2017.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: BLEU Metric — MT Goes Automatic
milestones.author: Kishore Papineni et al., IBM
milestones.summary: BLEU compares MT output against human reference translations using modified n-gram precision plus a brevity penalty.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made MT research reproducible at scale. 25+ years of standard evaluation. The metric's dominance also created problems — researchers optimized for BLEU rather than human judgment.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: Neural Probabilistic Language Model
milestones.author: Yoshua Bengio et al., Université de Montréal
milestones.summary: Bengio et al. trained a feed-forward neural network to predict the next word given the previous n words. Each word was mapped to a learned distributed representation (a 100-dim vector) before being fed to the network.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Combined two ideas that became the foundation of modern NLP: distributed word representations + neural language modeling. Anticipated word2vec by 10 years and contextual embeddings by 15.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: Statistical Machine Translation Goes Mainstream
milestones.author: Philipp Koehn et al. (Moses); Franz Och (Google Translate)
milestones.summary: 2005-2006 was the inflection point for SMT. Koehn released Moses, making phrase-based SMT accessible to any researcher. Google Translate launched in April 2006.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made working translation systems a real product. Set the stage for the neural MT revolution. Phrase-based paradigm dominated 2005-2015.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

eras.label: Embeddings & Deep Learning Era
eras.summary: Neural networks returned to NLP. word2vec, GloVe, seq2seq, attention, and the rise of NMT.

milestones.title: word2vec — Distributed Word Vectors Go Mainstream
milestones.author: Tomáš Mikolov, Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, Jeff Dean — Google
milestones.summary: CBOW and Skip-gram architectures produced vectors where semantic relationships appeared as linear offsets ('king − man + woman ≈ queen'). Trained on 100B words.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made word embeddings practical at web scale. Became a default preprocessing step in nearly every NLP pipeline 2014-2017.

links.label: Wikipedia: Efficient estimation of word representations
Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: Seq2Seq + Attention
milestones.author: Sutskever, Vinyals, Le (Google); Bahdanau, Cho, Bengio
milestones.summary: Encoder-decoder LSTM + attention for MT. Attention lets the decoder look back at all encoder states with learned weights.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Attention directly paved the way for the Transformer (2017). Without it, no GPT, BERT, or modern LLMs.

links.label: Wikipedia: Attention Is All You Need
Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: GloVe — Global Vectors
milestones.author: Pennington, Socher, Manning — Stanford
milestones.summary: Learns embeddings by factorizing the global word-word co-occurrence matrix.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Provided a complementary method to word2vec. Standard pre-trained embeddings (50d-300d) freely available.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: TensorFlow Released
milestones.author: Google Brain
milestones.summary: Open-sourced deep learning framework. Combined graph-based computation with auto-diff and GPU acceleration.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Democratized deep learning research. Dominant framework for NLP 2015-2019, before PyTorch overtook.

milestones.title: Google Neural Machine Translation (GNMT)
milestones.author: Wu et al., Google
milestones.summary: 8-layer encoder + 8-layer decoder LSTM with attention + residual connections. Deployed in production.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Proved NMT worked at production scale. Within a year Google Translate switched from SMT to GNMT.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

eras.label: Transformer / LLM Era
eras.summary: Self-attention replaced recurrence. Pretrain-then-finetune. Model size and data scale became dominant.

milestones.title: Transformer — 'Attention Is All You Need'
milestones.author: Vaswani et al., Google Brain & Research
milestones.summary: Replaced recurrence and convolutions with stacked self-attention + feedforward. Parallelizable, faster, stronger on MT.
milestones.why_it_mattered: The architecture underlying every modern LLM. By 2024, 100k+ citations.

milestones.title: BERT + GPT-1
milestones.author: Devlin et al. (Google); Radford et al. (OpenAI)
milestones.summary: BERT is encoder-only transformer with masked language modeling. GPT-1 is decoder-only with left-to-right LM.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Defined the pretrain-finetune paradigm. Within 18 months every SOTA NLP benchmark was held by a transformer.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: GPT-2 + XLNet + RoBERTa + T5
milestones.author: OpenAI, Google Brain, Facebook AI
milestones.summary: Cambrian explosion of transformer variants. GPT-2 (1.5B). T5 cast all NLP tasks as text-to-text.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Established that scale + data + training reliably improved quality. Empirical scaling-laws foundation.

links.label: Wikipedia: History of natural language processing

milestones.title: GPT-3 — In-Context Learning Emerges
milestones.author: Brown et al., OpenAI
milestones.summary: 175B-parameter decoder-only transformer. 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' demonstrated in-context learning.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Showed emergent capabilities. Triggered commercial LLM race. Demonstrated scaling laws.

milestones.author: OpenAI
milestones.summary: Released Nov 30, 2022. GPT-3.5 fine-tuned with RLHF. 100M users in 2 months.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Brought LLMs to the public. Sparked the 2023 generative AI boom. RLHF became standard alignment.

milestones.title: GPT-4 + Claude 2 + Llama 2 — Multimodal Year
milestones.author: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta
milestones.summary: GPT-4 added image inputs. Claude 2 launched with 100k context. Llama 2 released openly.

milestones.author: Anthropic, OpenAI
milestones.summary: Claude 3.5 Sonnet topped coding benchmarks. o1 (Sep 2024) introduced test-time compute reasoning.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Test-time compute scaling emerged as new axis. Reasoning chains and search became first-class.

milestones.author: DeepSeek (Hangzhou, China)
milestones.summary: Matched or exceeded OpenAI o1 on reasoning benchmarks. Open-weight license.

milestones.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
milestones.author: Anthropic
milestones.summary: Open standard for connecting LLMs to data sources, tools, and agents. USB-C for AI.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Standardized tool use across models. By 2025, OpenAI and Google both adopted MCP.

milestones.title: Frontier Reasoning + Agentic Workflows
milestones.author: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta
milestones.summary: Frontier models combine test-time reasoning, MCP tool use, long context, multimodality, and agentic loops.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Field moved from 'chat with a model' to 'coordinate an agent'. 9-year trajectory since Transformer paper.

milestones.title: Tier-1 Reasoning Frontier
milestones.author: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI
milestones.summary: Frontier reasoning models surpassed PhD-level reasoning on most benchmarks. MMLU Pro, GPQA Diamond, AMC 12 at 90%+.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Validated scaling laws continued past GPT-4. Sparked AGI timeline debates.

milestones.author: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Microsoft, Apple

milestones.why_it_mattered: Shifted 'app store' paradigm. Agents became universal interface. Workforce disruption in clerical/engineering roles.
